# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:53:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).

  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs

  = deny).

  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:53:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:53:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:53:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:53:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

// The check rides BEFORE the gate so it costs nothing when

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:53:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

LedgerSnapshotThrottle({

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:53:58Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps

But careful: the trailing-leg Timer leg — with a frozen clock, `poll()` never returns true (elapsed < interval), so the trailing flush never fires from the Timer... but the test asserts ≤2 records where the second comes from... hmm, wait. Let me re-check: in the wiring test, the ≤2 records: (a) the first mutation (job start 1) persists; (b) the finalize `_persistJobBoard()` unforced... wait that's unforced and inside the window → refused. The flush force at shutdown: `runHeadless` finally calls `_flushJobBoardPersist()` which force-persists → record 2. So 2 records: first + force-flush. With a frozen clock: mutation 1 → persists (never persisted). confirmPersisted stamps `_lastPersistAt = clock()`. Mutations 2..8 → refused (frozen clock: difference = 0 < 30s) → pending reserved, timer armed (real 30s Timer, but run ends before it fires; and the finally disposes). Force flush at shutdown → record 2. Same behavior, fully deterministic. 

Also the trailing flush never firing with a frozen clock is fine for this test since the force-flush covers the final state.

1. `AgentCliConfig` field — the config is the natural carrier for tunables, but it's a data class; is it used for test seams elsewhere? Let me check what's in AgentCliConfig. Actually `waitingClock`/`waitingSleep` are constructor params on AgentCli, not config fields. So the established seam pattern is constructor params on AgentCli.

2. But hold on — maybe simpler: the throttle field initializer could read an overridable getter, e.g. `Duration get ledgerSnapshotPersistIntervalOverride => ledgerSnapshotPersistInterval;`? That's hacky.

I'll follow the established pattern: constructor params on `AgentCli`:

/// pinned clock makes the wiring pin deterministic (a CI stall cannot
/// open a second window mid-test).
DateTime Function()? jobBoardLedgerClock,
```

```dart

  clock: jobBoardLedgerClock,
  onFlushDue: () => unawaited(_persistJobBoard()),
);
```

Then the wiring test passes `jobBoardLedgerClock: () => DateTime(2026, 10, 13, 12)` — a frozen clock. The mutation-refusal path never opens a second window regardless of real time.

Hmm, but wait: there's a subtlety with the throttle + deduper interplay in the wiring test with a frozen clock. Sequence in the headless run:
1. Job 1 starts → `_persistJobBoard()` → records non-empty → gate: never persisted → persist. json = board state 1. deduper.shouldPersist → true. append. confirm both. → record 1.
2. Jobs 2-4 start → gate refuses (frozen clock, last = t0) → pending reserved.
