# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place

  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

# pr-1594: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

Now I have a full picture. Let me plan the work:

## Fixes (5 inline threads + 1 IMPORTANT):

### Thread 1 — `agent_hub_cli.dart` comment rationale inverted
Reword the comment per the reviewer's suggestion:
```dart
// BEFORE the gate: an empty board must neither append nor stamp the
// window — an empty snapshot persisting would gate the first real
// snapshot for a whole interval. The toRecords() cost on refused
// mutations is a capped-list copy, not an encode.
```
Non-behavioral: no test needed.

### Thread 2 — `session_repair.dart` duplicated doc line
Drop one `/// Human-readable summary lines for a CLI report.` line. Non-behavioral.

### Thread 3 — `session_repair.dart` braces on `if (bytes >= (1 << 10))`
Add braces. Verified by `dart analyze` being clean. Non-behavioral.

### Thread 4 — `ledger_caps.dart` `prefer_initializing_formals`
`_onFlushDue = onFlushDue;` trips the lint. Options: use `this._onFlushDue` initializing formal (Dart ≥2.17 supports private named initializing formals — the public parameter name is derived by stripping the underscore: `onFlushDue`). That's exactly the lint's preferred fix and keeps the API identical. Let me check the SDK constraint in pubspec.yaml to be sure `this._onFlushDue` is available (needs Dart 2.17+).

Wait — one nuance: `_onFlushDue` field is declared `final void Function()? _onFlushDue;` mid-class. With an initializing formal, the parameter becomes `this._onFlushDue` with type inferred from the field or declared inline: `void Function()? _onFlushDue` hmm no. The syntax is:

```dart
LedgerSnapshotThrottle({
  this.minInterval = ledgerSnapshotPersistInterval,
  DateTime Function()? clock,
  void Function()? onFlushDue,
});
```

Wait, for private named fields: `LedgerSnapshotThrottle({this._onFlushDue})` — is that valid? Yes, since Dart 2.17: "you can use private fields initializing formals; the parameter name is the public name (underscore stripped)". Hmm, actually wait — I need to double check: Dart 2.17 release notes: "Constructor parameters can now refer to private fields with this._private syntax"? Let me think...

Actually I recall precisely now: Dart 2.17 added "generic enhanced enums"... and the private-final initializing formals feature — I'm fairly confident it exists. From the Dart language tour: "Initializing formal parameters can also be used for private fields: `class X { final String _name; X(this._name); }` — here the parameter name is `name` (without underscore)". Hmm, but for NAMED parameters: `X({this._name})` creates a named parameter called `name`. Yes, this is supported since Dart 2.17.

But hold on — there's a subtlety: the lint `prefer_initializing_formals` historically did NOT fire for private fields because `this._x` wasn't allowed; newer versions fire and the fix is `this._onFlushDue`. Since the review says the lint fires, the SDK supports the fix.

Alternatively, the reviewer's second option: "rename the parameter to match the field convention used by the liveness trackers this class mirrors". Let me check what the liveness trackers do — the CLI has liveness trackers with clock seams. Let me find them.

Actually, let me just check what the analyzer says and try `this._onFlushDue`. But first check the pubspec SDK constraint.

### Thread 5 — wall-clock dependency in wiring test
Make the pin deterministic. Options:
- Add a `clock` seam to the throttle wiring in the CLI (constructor param on AgentCli, e.g. `jobBoardLedgerClock`), then the test pins the clock so the window never elapses.
- Add an interval override.

Which is more consistent with the codebase? The `AgentCli` constructor already has `waitingClock` and `waitingSleep` seams. The `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` takes both `minInterval` and `clock`. The wiring test drives `runHeadless`; all 8 mutations must land in one window. A pinned clock (`() => fixedTime`) makes `shouldPersistNow()` always true on first and refused after — deterministic.

But careful: the trailing-leg Timer leg — with a frozen clock, `poll()` never returns true (elapsed < interval), so the trailing flush never fires from the Timer... but the test asserts ≤2 records where the second comes from... hmm, wait. Let me re-check: in the wiring test, the ≤2 records: (a) the first mutation (job start 1) persists; (b) the finalize `_persistJobBoard()` unforced... wait that's unforced and inside the window → refused. The flush force at shutdown: `runHeadless` finally calls `_flushJobBoardPersist()` which force-persists → record 2. So 2 records: first + force-flush. With a frozen clock: mutation 1 → persists (never persisted). confirmPersisted stamps `_lastPersistAt = clock()`. Mutations 2..8 → refused (frozen clock: difference = 0 < 30s) → pending reserved, timer armed (real 30s Timer, but run ends before it fires; and the finally disposes). Force flush at shutdown → record 2. Same behavior, fully deterministic. 

Also the trailing flush never firing with a frozen clock is fine for this test since the force-flush covers the final state.

Now — how to inject? Options:
1. `AgentCliConfig` field — the config is the natural carrier for tunables, but it's a data class; is it used for test seams elsewhere? Let me check what's in AgentCliConfig. Actually `waitingClock`/`waitingSleep` are constructor params on AgentCli, not config fields. So the established seam pattern is constructor params on AgentCli.

2. But hold on — maybe simpler: the throttle field initializer could read an overridable getter, e.g. `Duration get ledgerSnapshotPersistIntervalOverride => ledgerSnapshotPersistInterval;`? That's hacky.

I'll follow the established pattern: constructor params on `AgentCli`:
```dart
/// gh-1590: the job-board ledger persist window seam for tests — a
/// pinned clock makes the wiring pin deterministic (a CI stall cannot
/// open a second window mid-test).
DateTime Function()? jobBoardLedgerClock,
```
and the field:
```dart
late final LedgerSnapshotThrottle _jobBoardPersistThrottle = LedgerSnapshotThrottle(
  clock: jobBoardLedgerClock,
  onFlushDue: () => unawaited(_persistJobBoard()),
);

Now I have a full picture. Let me plan the work:

## Fixes (5 inline threads + 1 IMPORTANT):

### Thread 1 — `agent_hub_cli.dart` comment rationale inverted
Reword the comment per the reviewer's suggestion:
```dart
// BEFORE the gate: an empty board must neither append nor stamp the
// window — an empty snapshot persisting would gate the first real
// snapshot for a whole interval. The toRecords() cost on refused
// mutations is a capped-list copy, not an encode.
```
Non-behavioral: no test needed.

### Thread 2 — `session_repair.dart` duplicated doc line
Drop one `/// Human-readable summary lines for a CLI report.` line. Non-behavioral.

### Thread 3 — `session_repair.dart` braces on `if (bytes >= (1 << 10))`
Add braces. Verified by `dart analyze` being clean. Non-behavioral.

### Thread 4 — `ledger_caps.dart` `prefer_initializing_formals`
`_onFlushDue = onFlushDue;` trips the lint. Options: use `this._onFlushDue` initializing formal (Dart ≥2.17 supports private named initializing formals — the public parameter name is derived by stripping the underscore: `onFlushDue`). That's exactly the lint's preferred fix and keeps the API identical. Let me check the SDK constraint in pubspec.yaml to be sure `this._onFlushDue` is available (needs Dart 2.17+).

Wait — one nuance: `_onFlushDue` field is declared `final void Function()? _onFlushDue;` mid-class. With an initializing formal, the parameter becomes `this._onFlushDue` with type inferred from the field or declared inline: `void Function()? _onFlushDue` hmm no. The syntax is:

```dart
LedgerSnapshotThrottle({
  this.minInterval = ledgerSnapshotPersistInterval,
  DateTime Function()? clock,
  void Function()? onFlushDue,
});
```

Wait, for private named fields: `LedgerSnapshotThrottle({this._onFlushDue})` — is that valid? Yes, since Dart 2.17: "you can use private fields initializing formals; the parameter name is the public name (underscore stripped)". Hmm, actually wait — I need to double check: Dart 2.17 release notes: "Constructor parameters can now refer to private fields with this._private syntax"? Let me think...

Actually I recall precisely now: Dart 2.17 added "generic enhanced enums"... and the private-final initializing formals feature — I'm fairly confident it exists. From the Dart language tour: "Initializing formal parameters can also be used for private fields: `class X { final String _name; X(this._name); }` — here the parameter name is `name` (without underscore)". Hmm, but for NAMED parameters: `X({this._name})` creates a named parameter called `name`. Yes, this is supported since Dart 2.17.

But hold on — there's a subtlety: the lint `prefer_initializing_formals` historically did NOT fire for private fields because `this._x` wasn't allowed; newer versions fire and the fix is `this._onFlushDue`. Since the review says the lint fires, the SDK supports the fix.

Alternatively, the reviewer's second option: "rename the parameter to match the field convention used by the liveness trackers this class mirrors". Let me check what the liveness trackers do — the CLI has liveness trackers with clock seams. Let me find them.

Actually, let me just check what the analyzer says and try `this._onFlushDue`. But first check the pubspec SDK constraint.

### Thread 5 — wall-clock dependency in wiring test
Make the pin deterministic. Options:
- Add a `clock` seam to the throttle wiring in the CLI (constructor param on AgentCli, e.g. `jobBoardLedgerClock`), then the test pins the clock so the window never elapses.
- Add an interval override.

Which is more consistent with the codebase? The `AgentCli` constructor already has `waitingClock` and `waitingSleep` seams. The `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` takes both `minInterval` and `clock`. The wiring test drives `runHeadless`; all 8 mutations must land in one window. A pinned clock (`() => fixedTime`) makes `shouldPersistNow()` always true on first and refused after — deterministic.

But careful: the trailing-leg Timer leg — with a frozen clock, `poll()` never returns true (elapsed < interval), so the trailing flush never fires from the Timer... but the test asserts ≤2 records where the second comes from... hmm, wait. Let me re-check: in the wiring test, the ≤2 records: (a) the first mutation (job start 1) persists; (b) the finalize `_persistJobBoard()` unforced... wait that's unforced and inside the window → refused. `_onFlushDue = onFlushDue;` trips the lint. Options: use `this._onFlushDue` initializing formal (Dart ≥2.17 supports private named initializing formals — the public parameter name is derived by stripping the underscore: `onFlushDue`). That's exactly the lint's preferred fix and keeps the API identical. Let me check the SDK constraint in pubspec.yaml to be sure `this._onFlushDue` is available (needs Dart 2.17+).

Wait — one nuance: `_onFlushDue` field is declared `final void Function()? _onFlushDue;` mid-class. With an initializing formal, the parameter becomes `this._onFlushDue` with type inferred from the field or declared inline: `void Function()? _onFlushDue` hmm no. The syntax is:

```dart
LedgerSnapshotThrottle({
  this.minInterval = ledgerSnapshotPersistInterval,

});
```

Wait, for private named fields: `LedgerSnapshotThrottle({this._onFlushDue})` — is that valid? Hmm, actually wait — I need to double check: Dart 2.17 release notes: "Constructor parameters can now refer to private fields with this._private syntax"? Let me think...

Actually I recall precisely now: Dart 2.17 added "generic enhanced enums"... and the private-final initializing formals feature — I'm fairly confident it exists. From the Dart language tour: "Initializing formal parameters can also be used for private fields: `class X { final String _name; X(this._name); }` — here the parameter name is `name` (without underscore)". Hmm, but for NAMED parameters: `X({this._name})` creates a named parameter called `name`. Yes, this is supported since Dart 2.17.

But hold on — there's a subtlety: the lint `prefer_initializing_formals` historically did NOT fire for private fields because `this._x` wasn't allowed; newer versions fire and the fix is `this._onFlushDue`. Since the review says the lint fires, the SDK supports the fix.

`_onFlushDue = onFlushDue;` trips the lint. Options: use `this._onFlushDue` initializing formal (Dart ≥2.17 supports private named initializing formals — the public parameter name is derived by stripping the underscore: `onFlushDue`). That's exactly the lint's preferred fix and keeps the API identical. Let me check the SDK constraint in pubspec.yaml to be sure `this._onFlushDue` is available (needs Dart 2.17+).

Wait — one nuance: `_onFlushDue` field is declared `final void Function()? _onFlushDue;` mid-class. With an initializing formal, the parameter becomes `this._onFlushDue` with type inferred from the field or declared inline: `void Function()? _onFlushDue` hmm no. The syntax is:

```dart
LedgerSnapshotThrottle({
  this.minInterval = ledgerSnapshotPersistInterval,
  DateTime Function()? clock,

```

Wait, for private named fields: `LedgerSnapshotThrottle({this._onFlushDue})` — is that valid? Hmm, actually wait — I need to double check: Dart 2.17 release notes: "Constructor parameters can now refer to private fields with this._private syntax"? Let me think...

Actually I recall precisely now: Dart 2.17 added "generic enhanced enums"... and the private-final initializing formals feature — I'm fairly confident it exists. From the Dart language tour: "Initializing formal parameters can also be used for private fields: `class X { final String _name; X(this._name); }` — here the parameter name is `name` (without underscore)". Hmm, but for NAMED parameters: `X({this._name})` creates a named parameter called `name`. Yes, this is supported since Dart 2.17.

But hold on — there's a subtlety: the lint `prefer_initializing_formals` historically did NOT fire for private fields because `this._x` wasn't allowed; newer versions fire and the fix is `this._onFlushDue`. Since the review says the lint fires, the SDK supports the fix.

With a frozen clock: mutation 1 → persists (never persisted). confirmPersisted stamps `_lastPersistAt = clock()`. Mutations 2..8 → refused (frozen clock: difference = 0 < 30s) → pending reserved, timer armed (real 30s Timer, but run ends before it fires; and the finally disposes). Also the trailing flush never firing with a frozen clock is fine for this test since the force-flush covers the final state.

A clock seam (`DateTime Function()? jobBoardLedgerClock`) — frozen clock. Alternatively `Duration? jobBoardPersistInterval` widened to e.g. 1 hour. Both work. Hmm — but there's a subtle race: the Timer was armed at the FIRST refusal (mutation 1 of the coalesced batch) — it fires 40ms after that, possibly BEFORE I advance the clock (if the mutations + my code take >40ms real). Then poll() at fire time: clock frozen → 0 < 40ms → false → return, and `_timer = null` already — the leg DISARMS without flushing! Then I advance the clock and wait — nothing re-arms (no new refusal). Test flaky!

Hmm. Fix: advance the clock BEFORE the leg can fire? The mutations take microseconds; the leg fires 40ms later. Sequence: mutations (t≈0ms real) → advance clock + await 120ms → leg fires at 40ms real with clock already advanced → flush. The advance happens at ~0-1ms real — well before 40ms. Race exists only if the test thread stalls >40ms between the mutations and the advance — on a loaded CI, possible! But if the leg fired BEFORE the clock advance and disarmed WITHOUT flushing, then flushPersist force-appends → +1 anyway. Either path: exactly +1. So: assert `snapshots.length == afterCoalesced + 1` after `await manager.flushPersist()` following the advance+delay, and separately assert the final state. Even simpler: drop the delicate trailing-leg real-timer dance from THIS test; test the trailing leg deterministically at the throttle level (already covered in shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart). The wasted-fire case: leg fired at 40ms real while seam frozen → poll false → leg disarms → advancing later does nothing → flushPersist covers the final state (dedupe) → my assertion "final state reached" still holds but "+1 exactly" holds too (leg no-op'd, flush +1; or leg flushed +1, flush deduped). So turn-boundary `update()` persists are load-bearing for resume correctness: an interrupted mid-run child's usage must survive restart. Coalescing `update()` breaks that invariant.

Hmm. So how do I apply the throttle to SubagentManager without breaking this?

Options:
1. `update()` persists FORCEd (bypass window), while other mutation paths (touch — already in-memory; message delivery `_touchWithMessage`; recordReply; recordCompaction; attachSession) coalesce. Turn boundaries are per-child-request — a long-running child doing hundreds of requests appends hundreds of snapshots — that's the "unbounded" complaint? Turn-boundary: once per child request — could be hundreds per child per long run. With force, unbounded at that rate. Hmm.

Coalescing means the file can lag by up to 30s/one window of turn updates. On crash-resume, the registry row shows the last PERSISTED usage — acceptable staleness? The #332 test pins "snapshot written after turn 1 must already carry the turn's usage". If I coalesce updates, that test needs semantic downgrade — that's overriding a deliberate issue-#332 invariant. Risky scope creep.

Decision: throttle SubagentManager's PERSIST at the paths that are NOT the issue-#332 turn-billing path and NOT status transitions. I.e.:

### Test 1: obligations ledger throttle wiring test (new file)

I'll model it on the pending-wait/close-obligation harness: REPL conversation with 5 classifying asks, frozen `ledgerClock`, then scan the file.

Assertions:
- `records.length ≤ 2` — the first ingest + the teardown flush (RED: 5).
- The LAST record carries all 5 asks.
- Determinism: frozen clock → no second window regardless of runner stalls.

Also a second test: the coalesced entries must reach the file even when the REPL exits right after (the teardown flush) — that's covered by test 1's last-record assertion.

Wait — one wrinkle: with the FROZEN clock, `confirmPersisted` stamps t0. First ingest appends. Ingests 2-5 refused. REPL `/exit` → `_teardownAfterRepl` → `_flushObligationsLedger` → force → dedupe (differs) → append final (5 entries). Total 2. 

But WAIT — will `_ingestObligations` even fire per message here? It fires on PERSISTED UserMessages (REPL lines). Yes — each `io.sendLine` → `_persistIncremental` → `_ingestObligations`. The 'please ...' lines classify (openAsk). The first line 'begin' classifies nothing.

Order in the file: the obligations records interleave with messages; readCustomRecordsOfType returns in file order; `.last` = the final flush.

New group with:
1. RED main test: 4 registers (forced) then 8 coalesced mutations (4 recordReply + 4 recordCompaction) with a controllable clock → expect NO new snapshots while frozen; then advance clock + real delay for the trailing leg → exactly +1 snapshot carrying the final state; then flushPersist → no more.

4. flushPersist dedupe: flush twice → still N snapshots.

Hmm — test 1's trailing-leg: manager clock frozen during mutations, then advance by `persistInterval`, await 120ms real → trailing leg fires (Timer armed with 40ms REAL — wait, no! `Timer(minInterval, ...)` — the Timer uses minInterval = 40ms real. poll() checks the SEAM clock difference ≥ minInterval. So: freeze clock at t0 through the mutations; then `now = t0 + 40ms` (or +41), await 120ms real → leg fires → poll: 40ms ≥ 40ms → true → flush. 

Hmm — but there's a subtle race: the Timer was armed at the FIRST refusal (mutation 1 of the coalesced batch) — it fires 40ms after that, possibly BEFORE I advance the clock (if the mutations + my code take >40ms real). Then poll() at fire time: clock frozen → 0 < 40ms → false → return, and `_timer = null` already — the leg DISARMS without flushing! Then I advance the clock and wait — nothing re-arms (no new refusal). Test flaky!

Hmm. Fix: advance the clock BEFORE the leg can fire? The mutations take microseconds; the leg fires 40ms later. Sequence: mutations (t≈0ms real) → advance clock + await 120ms → leg fires at 40ms real with clock already advanced → flush. The advance happens at ~0-1ms real — well before 40ms. Race exists only if the test thread stalls >40ms between the mutations and the advance — on a loaded CI, possible! Robustify: after advancing, if the leg already consumed itself, the `flushPersist()` fallback covers it — but then my exact-count assertion (`+1`) breaks if BOTH fire (leg + manual flush → dedupe suppresses the second → still +1 total!). flushPersist is force → deduper suppresses the byte-identical no-op → count stays +1. But if the leg fired BEFORE the clock advance and disarmed WITHOUT flushing, then flushPersist force-appends → +1 anyway. Either path: exactly +1. So: assert `snapshots.length == afterCoalesced + 1` after `await manager.flushPersist()` following the advance+delay, and separately assert the final state. Even simpler: drop the delicate trailing-leg real-timer dance from THIS test; test the trailing leg deterministically at the throttle level (already covered in shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart). In the MANAGER test: freeze everything; mutations coalesce (assert 0 new); `await manager.flushPersist()` → exactly +1 with the final state; flush again → +0 (dedupe). The trailing-leg production wiring (`onFlushDue: _persist`) — covered how? The wiring is `onFlushDue: _persist` — a one-liner; the throttle's own tests cover poll→onFlushDue. And I can add a manager-level trailing test with `persistInterval: 40ms` + REAL clock (no seam) + real delay: 8 coalesced mutations with the REAL clock all within 40ms?? Race-y on a loaded runner — the exact wall-clock fragility thread 5 complains about. NO. Alternative deterministic trailing test via the clock seam: mutations frozen; advance clock; then pump microtasks?? The leg is a REAL Timer(minInterval) armed at refusal — 40ms real. After advancing the seam, await 120ms real: fires IF not already fired-and-wasted. The wasted-fire case: leg fired at 40ms real while seam frozen → poll false → leg disarms → advancing later does nothing → flushPersist covers the final state (dedupe) → my assertion "final state reached" still holds but "+1 exactly" holds too (leg no-op'd, flush +1; or leg flushed +1, flush deduped). Either way +1. 

So the deterministic assertion set:
1. After 8 coalesced mutations (clock frozen): snapshots.length == afterRegistration (nothing appended).
2. Advance seam clock by ≥ persistInterval; await 120ms real (leg may or may not have fired productively); `await manager.flushPersist()`; snapshots.length == afterRegistration + 1; last snapshot carries every final state.
3. `await manager.flushPersist()` again → still +1 (dedupe).

This is fully deterministic and exercises the real leg when timing allows.

    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
